slides.title:
Root cause is usually
a *decision*, not a device.
slides.body:
Five whys stops the moment the
honest answer names a tradeoff.

slides.title: The supervisor failed
slides.body: Why did that take the site down?

slides.title: The redundant path
slides.body:
Wasn't carrying the routes
it was supposed to.

slides.title: Why not?
slides.body:
A config changed during a migration
and *never reverted*.

slides.title: Why wasn't it caught?
slides.body:
Validation was dropped when the
maintenance window got compressed.

slides.title: Why was it compressed?
slides.body:
*That's where the document ends.*
The finding reads "hardware failure."

slides.title: But the chain was still going
slides.body:
A fixed business deadline. A real risk
weighed against a real cost.
A choice that was probably *right*.

slides.title: Naming it isn't blame
slides.body:
You cannot buy a supervisor that
survives having its redundancy
*silently removed*.

slides.title: Postmortems that change anything
steps: Record the constraint, not just the event.
A reasonable decision can still cause an outage.

slides.title:
It found where the
failure surfaced.
